The ''o''-form may have also been reinforced by {{der|en|fro|long}}, from {{der|en|la|longus}}, from the same Indo-European word. {{doublet|en|lungo}} and {{m|en|lunge}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|lang||Northumbrian}} ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er,more}} # {{senseid|en|lengthy}} Having much [[distance]] in space from one end to the other. #: {{ux|en|I need a '''long''' piece of wood.}} #: {{ux|en|It’s a '''long''' way from the Earth to the Moon.}} #: {{ux|en|How '''long''' was your newborn baby?}} ## Specifically, having much distance in a [[horizontal]] dimension (''see also Usage Notes below''). ##: {{ux|en|This table is '''long''' but not very high.}} ## Travelling a great distance. ##: {{ux|en|Smith hoofs a '''long''' ball up to Jones.}} ## {{lb|en|informal}} Having a long [[penis]]. ##: {{ux|en|My ex was very strong but not very '''long'''.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=We expressed our readiness, and in ten minutes were in the station wagon, rolling rapidly down the '''long''' drive, for it was then after nine. No fam, I’m already gone.}} # {{lb|en|between ''have'' and a past participle}} A long time ago. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1918|author=James George Frazer|title=Folk-Lore In The Old Testament|volume=1|page=7|text=The place was solitary and deserted {{...}} only the line of mouldering towers and battlements on the hill above spoke of the busy life that had '''long''' passed away.}} =====Usage notes===== The use of ''long'' with the sense ''a long time'' (found as a complement of verbs like {{m|en|take}}, {{m|en|have}} ({{m|en|got}}), {{m|en|need}}, {{m|en|spend}}, {{m|en|give}}, {{m|en|be}} or of the prepositions {{m|en|for}} or {{m|en|before}}) is normally restricted to questions and negative statements.{{cite-book|last1=Pullum|first1=Geoffrey K.|last2=Huddleston|first2=Rodney|year=2002|chapter=Adjectives and adverbs|page=569|title=The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language}} In other situations, the phrase ''a long time'' is used instead: : ''Does it take '''long'''?'' :: ''— No, it doesn't take '''long'''.'' :: {{q|nonstandard}} ''— Yes, it takes '''long'''.'' :: ''— Yes, it takes '''a long time'''.'' :: ''— Yes, it takes far too '''long'''.'' This restriction does not apply when "long" is modified by an adverb such as ''too'' or ''enough''. It also does not apply when "long" is used as a premodifier of a verb, participle, adjective, preposition or adverb with the sense "for a long time". =====Derived terms===== {{col2|en|a creaking door hangs long on its hinges|long live|long lost|long since|one should live so long|since long|take long|go long}} =====Translations===== {{see translation subpage|Adverb}} =====See also===== * {{l|en|far}} * {{l|en|wide}} * {{l|en|broad}} ===Etymology 3=== From {{inh|en|enm|longen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|langian||to long for, yearn after, grieve for, be pained, lengthen, grow longer, summon, belong}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*langōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*langōną||to desire, long for}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lengʷʰ-||to be easy, be quick, jump, move around, vary}}.
